text: Twenty videos end here: Wrenfield went from no central way to answer HR, IT, and Ops questions to a real assistant that cites its sources and knows when to say it doesn't know.
Along the way, a real prompt-injection incident was found and fixed through the team's own red-team review -- not luck.
Three honest gaps get named: no continuous monitoring for new injection attempts, no automated re-indexing on source changes, and no agent that can act on anyone's behalf yet.
A short next-phase list follows: grow eval coverage first, then automate re-indexing, then scope the agent idea carefully, with a human still approving every action.
That's the honest finish line -- a real assistant, a real incident handled well, and real limits handed off instead of hidden. Series complete.
